title: omakase-ee-provider/1
description: The manifest of one release of a D1 end-effector provider: the package that carries it, the SDK contract it serves, how a side's unit runs it, the configuration it reads, the models it drives and the conformance run that passed. A robot's fit document references a provider by `{id, version}`; the manifest is complete offline, read from a local file or from a hub registry. Rules a JSON Schema cannot state (the conformance harness inside the SDK range, `{side}` as the only placeholder, the program path, the registry key's file name, posture lengths) are checked by `d1fw-ee-manifest check`. A provider that reads no configuration file names none of `launch.config_dir`, `launch.config_file` and `config_schema`, and needs no calibration; one that reads one names all three.

schema.description: The document type and its major version.

id.description: A dotted namespace of two to six lowercase segments, by convention `d1-firmware.end-effector.<vendor>.<model>`: the name a fit document references the provider by, with `version`; for a provider the artifacts hub distributes, also its registry entry name.

version.description: The release, equal to the Debian package's version: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with no pre-release or build suffix.

package.description: The Debian package this release installs from. `plane: "apt"`: the package is installed by name and version from an apt source (the hub's signed apt suites, a vendor's own source) or is already installed with dpkg; the manifest names no bytes and needs no hub. `plane: "registry"`: the .deb is a content-addressed artifact on the hub's manifest plane, beside the manifest, and `key`, `sha256` and `sizeBytes` are its registry entry's fields; a consumer downloads `baseUrl + "/" + key`, checks the digest and the size, and installs it with dpkg. For `apt` the three fields are absent.

name.description: The package name as its control stanza spells it.

arch.description: The Debian architecture: `arm64` or `amd64` for a compiled program, `all` for an architecture-independent package.

plane.description: Where the package comes from: `apt` (an apt source or a local dpkg install) or `registry` (an artifact on the hub's manifest plane).

key.description: `plane: registry` only: the .deb's key relative to the hub's baseUrl (`<type>/<name>/<version>/<selector-values>/<filename>`), its file name `<name>_<version>_<arch>.deb`.

sha256.description: `plane: registry` only: the SHA-256 of the .deb, lowercase hex.

sizeBytes.description: `plane: registry` only: the size of the .deb, bytes.

sdk.description: What the provider was built against.

contract.description: The shared-memory contract the provider serves.

d1_ee_sdk.description: The d1-ee-sdk releases the provider builds with: one or more comparators joined by commas, all of which a release satisfies, e.g. ">=0.2.0, <0.3.0". A comparator is an operator (`>=`, `>`, `<=`, `<`, `=`, or none for `=`) and a plain MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version; spaces may surround the operator and the commas. No other range syntax is taken: no `^`, `~`, `*` or `x` wildcard, partial version, pre-release or build suffix, and no `||`. The fit's `provider.version` takes the same grammar.

command.description: The `EE_PROVIDER_COMMAND` template: an absolute program path `/opt/<package>/bin/<program>` and its arguments, words of ASCII letters, digits and `_./{}=:,@+-` separated by single spaces. `{side}` is the only placeholder and must appear; the program word holds none. The unit word-splits the value without a shell parse, so quotes, the backquote, `$ ; & | < > ( ) \ * ? ! ~ # %`, a tab, a newline and every non-ASCII character are outside the allowed set. The same expression is `COMMAND_PATTERN` in d1fw-ee-manifest and in d1-provisioning's reader.

config_dir.description: The directory of the provider's per-side configuration file: a directory of its own under `/etc`, each segment starting with a letter or digit, no placeholder, no trailing slash. The daemon's layer directory `/etc/d1-firmwared/config.d` (and below) and anything under `/etc/systemd*` or `/etc/apt*` are refused. Present exactly when `config_file` and `config_schema` are.

config_file.description: The file name of a side's configuration inside `config_dir`, ending in `.toml` (the file is TOML, and the name can then never be a unit's `<side>.env` beside it); `{side}` is the only placeholder and must appear. Present exactly when `config_dir` and `config_schema` are.

config_schema.description: A JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of the per-side configuration file, its TOML read as JSON. `$schema`, when present, names draft 2020-12. Absent for a provider that reads no configuration file, together with `launch.config_dir` and `launch.config_file`.

models.description: Every model this release drives, as its descriptor announces it.

guard_models.description: Every collision envelope id a descriptor of this release declares as `guard_model`.

calibration.description: Whether the provider needs a per-robot calibration.

required.description: `true`: the fit supplies a calibration file, appended to the side's configuration file; a provider that reads no configuration file needs none (`false`).

conformance.description: The conformance run this release passed.

version.description: The harness release the run used; inside `sdk.d1_ee_sdk`.

run_url.description: Optional: where the run that executed `conformance::lifecycle` against the released commit is recorded: an https URL of a CI run, an absolute path of a local run log, or a hex digest (the commit the run was made on, or the SHA-256 of its log). Nothing in a manifest needs a network to be read.

name.description: A descriptor name (model, driver, guard envelope id): at most 64 bytes, no whitespace or control character.

links.description: How the device can be reached: the arm's flange channel (relayed by the daemon), CAN or CAN FD on an interface of the robot's computer, a USB serial adapter, or Ethernet.

joints.description: The number of joints the descriptor declares for this model.

postures.description: Named joint postures, each one value per joint in the descriptor's joint order: a fraction of that joint's range, 0 its `min` and 1 its `max`. A model with joints names at least `open` and `closed`.
